Iterating the previous lemma yields the following result. Note that we implicitly use that the Nakayama automorphism preserves the
\mathbbm{Z}_{2}
-grading in order to simplify certain sign formulas, and use the fact that
({}_{t}a)^{\vee}={}_{t}(a^{\vee})
for
a\in A
and
t\geq 0
by
Lemma

2.1.3
to omit certain parentheses.

Lemma 10.3.3
.

Let
u\in U(\mathfrak{h})^{t}
,
1\leq k\leq d
, and
\alpha_{1},\dotsc,\alpha_{d}\in A
. The map

C^{r}_{k}:\mathcal{M}\otimes V^{\otimes d}\rightarrow\mathcal{M}\otimes V^{\otimes d}

satisfies

\displaystyle C^{r}_{k}\left(u\otimes 1\otimes v_{t_{1}}^{\alpha_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{t_{d}}^{\alpha_{d}}\right)

\displaystyle\hskip 36.135pt\equiv_{t+1}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(b_{1},\dotsc,b_{r})\in\mathtt{B}^{r}\end{subarray}}(-1)^{\heartsuit}\left(uh_{t_{k}}^{b_{1}}\dotsb h_{t_{k}}^{b_{r}}\right)\otimes 1\otimes v_{t_{1}}^{\alpha_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{t_{k-1}}^{\alpha_{k-1}}\otimes v_{t_{k}}^{z_{k}}\otimes v_{t_{k+1}}^{\alpha_{k+1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{t_{d}}^{\alpha_{d}},

where

\heartsuit=\heartsuit(\alpha_{1},\dotsc,\alpha_{d};b_{1},\dotsc,b_{r})=\bar{\alpha}_{k}\bar{b}_{1}+(\bar{\alpha}_{k}+\bar{b}_{1})\bar{b}_{2}+\dotsb+(\bar{\alpha}_{k}+\dotsb+\bar{b}_{r-1})\bar{b}_{r}+(\bar{b}_{1}+\dotsb+\bar{b}_{r})(\bar{\alpha}_{1}+\dotsb+\bar{\alpha}_{k-1}),

and where

z_{k}=z_{k}(\alpha_{k};b_{1},\dotsc,b_{r}):=({}_{r}\alpha_{k})({}_{r-1}b_{1}^{\vee})({}_{r-2}b_{2}^{\vee})\dotsb({}_{1}b^{\vee}_{r-1})(b_{r}^{\vee}).

10.4.
On the image of thin diagrams under the defining representation

Let
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
be the full subcategory of
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}
consisting of objects which are words from the set
\left\{i^{(1)}\right\}_{i\in I}
. For short, for
i\in I
we will write
i
for
i^{(1)}
. By Corollary
6.4.2
,
{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d_{1}},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d_{2}})
is spanned by diagrams consisting only of thin strands involving affine dots, crossings, and coupons. In particular, if this morphism space is nonzero, then
d_{1}=d_{2}
.

For short, we will call a diagram
D
in
{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d})
a
normally ordered
diagram if it is an element of our putative basis. In particular,
D=X\circ C\circ T
, where
X
is a diagram that consists solely of crossings,
C
is a diagram that consists solely of coupons (with at most one on each strand), and
T
is a diagram that consists solely of affine dots. Given a normally ordered
D
in
{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d})
, let
\operatorname{undot}(D)
denote the diagram obtained from
D
by deleting the affine dots. For
k=1,\dotsc,d
, let
\beta_{k}(D)
equal the number of affine dots on the strand labeled by
i_{k}
on the bottom of
D
. In particular, if
x_{k}\in{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},i_{1}\dotsb i_{d})
is short for the diagram which has an affine dot on the
k
th strand, then for a normally ordered diagram
D
we have

(10.4.1)

D=\operatorname{undot}(D)\circ x_{d}^{\beta_{d}(D)}\circ\dotsb\circ x_{1}^{\beta_{1}(D)}.

Given a normally ordered diagram
D
in
{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d})
, let

\mathtt{B}^{\beta(D)}=\mathtt{B}^{\beta_{1}(D)}\times\dotsb\times\mathtt{B}^{\beta_{d}(D)},

and write
\mathbf{b}=(\mathbf{b}_{1},\dotsc,\mathbf{b}_{d})
for an element of
\mathtt{B}^{\beta(D)}
where
\mathbf{b}_{k}=(b_{k,1},\dotsc,b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)})\in\mathtt{B}^{\beta_{k}(D)}
.

Proposition 10.4.1
.

Let
D\in{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d})
be a normally ordered diagram and let
r=\sum_{k=1}^{d}\beta_{k}(D)
be the number of affine dots in
D
. Fix
n\geq d
. Consider the module homomorphism

H_{n}(D)_{\mathcal{M}}:\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{i_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{i_{d}}V\rightarrow\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V.

Then,

\displaystyle H_{n}(D)_{\mathcal{M}}\left(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}\right)

\displaystyle\hskip 0.0pt\equiv_{r}\sum_{\mathbf{b}\in\mathtt{B}^{\beta(D)}}(-1)^{\diamondsuit}h_{D}(\mathbf{b})\otimes 1\otimes G_{n}(\operatorname{undot}(D))\left(v_{1}^{z_{1}}\otimes v_{2}^{z_{2}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{z_{d}}\right),

where
h_{D}(\mathbf{b})\in U(\mathfrak{h})
is given by

\displaystyle h_{D}(\mathbf{b})

\displaystyle=\left(h_{1}^{b_{1,1}}h_{1}^{b_{1,2}}\dotsb h_{1}^{b_{1,\beta_{1}(D)}}\right)\left(h_{2}^{b_{2,1}}h_{2}^{b_{2,2}}\dotsb h_{2}^{b_{2,\beta_{2}(D)}}\right)\dotsb\left(h_{d}^{b_{d,1}}h_{d}^{b_{d,2}}\dotsb h_{d}^{b_{d,\beta_{d}(D)}}\right),

and where
\diamondsuit\in\mathbbm{Z}_{2}
is given by

\diamondsuit=\diamondsuit(i_{1},\dotsc,i_{d};\mathbf{b}):=\overline{D}\cdot\overline{h_{D}(\mathbf{b})}+\sum_{k=1}^{d}\heartsuit\left(z_{1},\dotsc,z_{k-1},i_{k},\dotsc,i_{d};b_{k,1},\dotsc,b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)}\right),

and where
z_{k}\in A
is given by

z_{k}=z_{k}(i_{k};\mathbf{b}_{k})=z_{k}(i_{k};b_{k,1},\dotsc,b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)}):=({}_{\beta_{k}(D)}i_{k})({}_{\beta_{k}(D)-1}b_{k,1}^{\vee})({}_{\beta_{k}(D)-2}b_{k,2}^{\vee})\dotsb({}_{1}b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)-1}^{\vee})(b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)}^{\vee}).

Proof.

The result follows by repeated applications of
Lemma

10.3.2
to compute the effect of the affine dots in the description of
D
given in (
10.4.1
) followed by the fact that the remainder of
D
, which equals
\operatorname{undot}(D)
, is a web without affine dots and so and acts on
V^{\otimes d}
, as indicated.
∎

10.5.
Decomposition of the associated graded module for
\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V

Observe that the PBW basis, filtrations, and results of the previous sections depend on a fixed choice of an ordered homogenous basis for
A
. However, these results can be applied to any choice of homogenous basis. Fix a totally ordered, homogeneous basis
\mathtt{B}
for
A
that contains
I
(e.g., a good basis for
A
). Let
\mathtt{B}^{\vee}
be the dual basis for
A
with ordering given by declaring
b_{1}^{\vee}\leq b_{2}^{\vee}
if and only if
b_{1}\leq b_{2}
. In what follows the PBW basis, filtrations, and the results of the previous sections will be taken with respect to the basis
\mathtt{B}^{\vee}
. In particular, replace references to elements of
\mathtt{B}
by references to elements of
\mathtt{B}^{\vee}
.

For example, using the ordered basis
\mathtt{B}^{\vee}
there is a PBW basis for
U(\mathfrak{h})
:

(10.5.1)

\left\{\left.\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}1\leq i\leq n\\
b\in\mathtt{B}\end{subarray}}\left(h^{b^{\vee}}_{i}\right)^{t_{i,b^{\vee}}}\right|1\leq i\leq n,b\in B,\text{ where }t_{i,b^{\vee}}\in\mathbbm{Z}\text{ if }\bar{b}=\bar{0},\text{ and }t_{i,b^{\vee}}\in\{0,1\}\text{ if }\bar{b}=\bar{1}\right\}.

Likewise, the ordered basis
\mathtt{B}^{\vee}
and arguments in the previous sections define a filtration on
\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V
. In particular, for any fixed
r\geq 0
the degree
r
component of the associated graded
\operatorname{gr}U(\mathfrak{h})
-module
\operatorname{gr}\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)
can be described as a
\mathbbm{k}
-module by

\displaystyle\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)^{\leq r}

\displaystyle/\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)^{\leq(r-1)}

\displaystyle\cong\left(\mathcal{M}^{\leq r}/\mathcal{M}^{\leq r-1}\right)\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V

\displaystyle\cong\left(U(\mathfrak{h})^{\leq r}/U(\mathfrak{h})^{\leq(r-1)}\right)\otimes U(\mathfrak{u}^{-})\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V

(10.5.2)

\displaystyle\cong\bigoplus_{X}X\otimes U(\mathfrak{u}^{-})\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V,

where the direct sum is over the PBW basis elements of
U(\mathfrak{h})
of degree
r
given in (
10.5.1
).

10.6.
Computation of the action of normally ordered diagrams in
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}

Using the previous results, we are now able to obtain enough information about the action of the homomorphism
H_{n}(D)_{\mathcal{M}}
to prove the normally ordered diagrams form a basis for the morphism spaces of
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
.

Fix a normally ordered diagram
D\in{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d})
. Reading from bottom-to-top,
D
consists of some number of affine dots on each strand, then a single coupon from
pAq
for some
p,q\in I
on each strand, then a diagram consisting of only crossings. Recall that
\beta_{k}=\beta_{k}(D)
denotes the number of affine dots on the
k
th strand of
D
. For
k=1,\dotsc,d
, let
\alpha_{k}\in j_{\tau^{-1}(k)}Ai_{k}
be the coupon on the
k
th strand of
D
, where
\tau
denotes both the subdiagram of the crossings at the top of
D
and the element of
S_{d}
that this diagram defines.

With this notation the description of
D
as
X\circ C\circ T
given in Section
10.4
can be expressed more explicitly as

(10.6.1)

D=\tau\circ\alpha_{1}\otimes\dotsb\otimes\alpha_{d}\circ x_{d}^{\beta_{d}}\circ\dotsb\circ x_{1}^{\beta_{1}}.

Recall that we assume
I\subseteq\mathtt{B}
. For
k=1,\dotsc,d
, let
\mathbf{b}_{k}\in I^{\beta_{k}(D)}\subseteq\mathtt{B}^{\beta_{k}(D)}
be given by

\mathbf{b}_{k}=(b_{k,1},\dotsc,b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)})=(i_{k},\dotsc,i_{k})\in I^{\beta_{k}(D)}\subseteq\mathtt{B}^{\beta_{k}(D)},

and

\mathbf{b}^{\vee}_{k}=(b^{\vee}_{k,1},\dotsc,b^{\vee}_{k,\beta_{k}(D)})=(i^{\vee}_{k},\dotsc,i_{k}^{\vee})\in(I^{\vee})^{\beta_{k}(D)}\subseteq(\mathtt{B}^{\vee})^{\beta_{k}(D)}.

Let
\mathbf{b}\in I^{\beta(D)}\subseteq\mathtt{B}^{\beta(D)}
be given by

(10.6.2)

\mathbf{b}=(\mathbf{b}_{1},\dotsc,\mathbf{b}_{d}),

and let
\mathbf{b}^{\vee}\in(I^{\vee})^{\beta(D)}\subseteq(\mathtt{B}^{\vee})^{\beta(D)}
be given by

(10.6.3)

\mathbf{b}^{\vee}=(\mathbf{b}^{\vee}_{1},\dotsc,\mathbf{b}^{\vee}_{d}).

For any fixed
\mathbf{c}\in(\mathtt{B}^{\vee})^{\beta(D)}
the discussion before (
10.6.4
) applied to
h_{D}(\mathbf{c})
defined in
10.4.1
implies that there is a unique PBW basis element
\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{c})}
of degree
r:=\sum_{k=1}^{d}\beta_{k}(D)
such that

(10.6.4)

h_{D}(\mathbf{c})\equiv_{r}\pm\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{c})}.

Observe that the set
\left\{v_{k}^{\alpha}\mid 1\leq k\leq n,\alpha\in{}_{j}\mathtt{B}\right\}
is a
\mathbbm{k}
-basis for
{}_{j}V
. More generally, if
\mathbb{Y}
is the set of PBW basis elements for
U(\mathfrak{u}^{-})
and
X
is a fixed PBW basis element of
U(\mathfrak{h})
, then the set

(10.6.5)

\left\{X\otimes Y\otimes v_{t_{1}}^{\alpha_{1}}\otimes\dotsb v_{t_{d}}^{\alpha_{d}}\mid Y\in\mathbb{Y},t_{k}\in[1,n]\text{ and }\alpha_{k}\in{}_{j_{k}}\mathtt{B}\text{ for $k=1,\dotsc,d$}\right\}

is a
\mathbbm{k}
-basis for the summand

X\otimes U(\mathfrak{u}^{-})\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V

in (
10.5
).

Theorem 10.6.1
.

Let
D\in{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d})
be a normally ordered diagram, let
r=\sum_{k=1}^{d}\beta_{k}(D)
be the total number of affine dots in
D
, and let
\mathbf{b}^{\vee}
be given by
Eq.

10.6.3
. Fix
n\geq d
. Consider the morphism

H_{n}(D)_{\mathcal{M}}:\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{i_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{i_{d}}V\rightarrow\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V.

Then, the image of
H_{n}(D)_{\mathcal{M}}\left(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}\right)
in the summand of (
10.5
) indexed by
\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}
equals

K_{D}\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}\otimes 1\otimes\left(v_{\tau^{-1}(1)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(1)}}\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(2)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(2)}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(d)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(d)}}\right),

where
K_{D}\in\mathbbm{k}
is nonzero and
\tau
,
\alpha_{1},\dotsc,\alpha_{d}
are as in
Eq.

10.6.1
.

Proof.

First, note that since
1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}
lies in
\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{i_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{i_{d}}V\right)^{0}
,
Proposition

10.4.1
implies
H_{n}(D)\left(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}\right)
lies in
\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)^{\leq r}
. Thus we can consider the image of this element in

\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)^{\leq r}/\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)^{\leq(r-1)}\cong\bigoplus_{X}X\otimes U(\mathfrak{u}^{-})\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V.

This element can further be projected onto the direct summand of (
10.5
) indexed by the PBW basis element
\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}
:

(10.6.6)

\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}\otimes U(\mathfrak{u}^{-})\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V.

Let
\mathcal{I}
be the image of
H_{n}(D)\left(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}\right)
in this summand.

We now show this image is as claimed. Let
\mathbb{X}\subseteq(\mathtt{B}^{\vee})^{\beta(D)}
be the set of all
\mathbf{c}\in(\mathtt{B}^{\vee})^{\beta(D)}
for which
c_{1,1},\dotsc,c_{d,\beta_{d}(D)}
equals
b^{\vee}_{1,1},\dotsc,b^{\vee}_{d,\beta_{d}(D)}
as an unordered list of elements from
\mathtt{B}^{\vee}
. It follows from (
10.6.4
) that the only terms in the sum given in Proposition
10.4.1
that contribute to summand indexed by
\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}
are those of the form
h_{D}(\mathbf{c})
for some
\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}
. Thus,
\mathcal{I}
equals the projection of

(10.6.7)

\sum_{\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}}(-1)^{\diamondsuit(i_{1},\dotsc,i_{d};\mathbf{c})}h_{D}(\mathbf{c})\otimes 1\otimes G_{n}(\operatorname{undot}(D))\left(v_{1}^{z_{1}}\otimes v_{2}^{z_{2}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{z_{d}}\right)

onto
Eq.

10.6.6
.

We next study the
z_{k}=z_{k}(i_{k};\mathbf{c}_{k})\in A
which appear in
Eq.

10.6.7
. Let
\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}
and let
c
be one of the entries of
\mathbf{c}
. Then
c=b_{p,q}^{\vee}=i_{p}^{\vee}
for some
p=1,\dotsc,d
and, since
(\ell^{\vee})^{\vee}=\ell
for any
\ell\in I
, we have:

{}_{t}(c^{\vee})={}_{t}((i_{k}^{\vee})^{\vee})=i_{k}\in I.

Therefore, each
z_{k}(i_{k};\mathbf{c}_{k})
is the product of
i_{k}\in I
along with potentially other elements of
I
. But
I
is a set of orthogonal idempotents. That is,
z_{k}(i_{k};\mathbf{c}_{k})
is either
i_{k}
or
0
.

Let
\mathbb{X}^{\prime}
be the set of all
\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}
for which
z_{k}(i_{k};\mathbf{c}_{k})=i_{k}
for all
k=1,\dotsc,d
. Since a summand in (
10.6.7
) is zero whenever
z_{k}(i_{k};\mathbf{c}_{k})=0
for some
k=1,\dotsc,d
, we may further assume that sum runs only over the elements of
\mathbb{X}^{\prime}
. Therefore, we have that
\mathcal{I}
is equal to the projection of:

\displaystyle=\sum_{\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}}(-1)^{\diamondsuit(i_{1},\dotsc,i_{d};\mathbf{c})}h_{D}(\mathbf{c})\otimes 1\otimes G_{n}(\operatorname{undot}(D))\left(v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes v_{2}^{i_{2}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}\right)

\displaystyle=\sum_{\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}}(-1)^{\diamondsuit(i_{1},\dotsc,i_{d};\mathbf{c})}h_{D}(\mathbf{c})\otimes 1\otimes G_{n}(\tau)\left(v_{1}^{\alpha_{1}}\otimes v_{2}^{\alpha_{2}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{\alpha_{d}}\right)

\displaystyle=\sum_{\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}}(-1)^{\diamondsuit(i_{1},\dotsc,i_{d};\mathbf{c})}h_{D}(\mathbf{c})\otimes 1\otimes\left(v_{\tau^{-1}(1)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(1)}}\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(2)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(2)}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(d)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(d)}}\right)

Note that since the elements of
I
are even, and both the Nakayama automorphism and the taking of the dual of an element preserve parity, it follows that the entries of
\mathbf{c}
are even for any
\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}
. This implies
\diamondsuit(i_{1},\dotsc,i_{d};\mathbf{c})=\bar{0}
for all
\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}
. It also implies

h_{D}(\mathbf{c})\equiv_{r}\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}

for all
\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}
. These observations allow further simplification. Namely,
\mathcal{I}
equals the projection of:

\displaystyle=\sum_{\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}}h_{D}(\mathbf{c})\otimes 1\otimes\left(v_{\tau^{-1}(1)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(1)}}\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(2)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(2)}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(d)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(d)}}\right)

\displaystyle=\sum_{\mathbf{c}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}}\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}\otimes 1\otimes\left(v_{\tau^{-1}(1)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(1)}}\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(2)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(2)}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(d)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(d)}}\right)

\displaystyle=\left|\mathbb{X}^{\prime}\right|\widetilde{h_{D}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}\otimes 1\otimes\left(v_{\tau^{-1}(1)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(1)}}\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(2)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(2)}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{\tau^{-1}(d)}^{\alpha_{\tau^{-1}(d)}}\right).

The claim follows once we verify
\mathbf{b}^{\vee}\in\mathbb{X}^{\prime}
. Since
\mathbf{b}^{\vee}
is obviously an element of
\mathbb{X}
, it remains to verify

\displaystyle z_{k}(i_{k};\mathbf{b}^{\vee}_{k})

\displaystyle=({}_{\beta_{k}(D)}i_{k})({}_{\beta_{k}(D)-1}(b_{k,1}^{\vee\vee}))({}_{\beta_{k}(D)-2}(b_{k,2}^{\vee\vee}))\dotsb({}_{1}(b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)-1}^{\vee\vee}))(b_{k,\beta_{k}(D)}^{\vee\vee})

\displaystyle=({}_{\beta_{k}(D)}i_{k})({}_{\beta_{k}(D)-1}(i_{k}))({}_{\beta_{k}(D)-2}(i_{k}))\dotsb({}_{1}(i_{k}))({}_{0}(i_{k})^{\vee\vee})

\displaystyle=(i_{k})(i_{k})(i_{k})\dotsb(i_{k})(i_{k})

\displaystyle=i_{k}.

∎

Theorem 10.6.2
.

Let

\sum_{t=1}^{p}\nu_{t}D_{t}\in{\rm Hom}_{\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}}(i_{1}\dotsb i_{d},j_{1}\dotsb j_{d})

be a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination of normally ordered diagrams. Let
n\geq d
. If
H_{n}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{p}\nu_{t}D_{t}\right)=0
, then
\nu_{t}=0
for
t=1,\dotsc,p
.

Proof.

Assume
\sum_{t=1}^{p}\nu_{t}D_{t}
is a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination of distinct normally ordered diagrams with
\nu_{t}\neq 0
for all
t=1,\dotsc,p
. Further assume that
H_{n}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{p}\nu_{t}D_{t}\right)=0
for some
n\geq d
. Then,

H_{n}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{p}\nu_{t}D_{t}\right)_{\mathcal{M}}:\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{i_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{i_{d}}V\rightarrow\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V.

is the zero map.

Without loss of generality, we may assume
D_{1}
is the diagram in the sum with the greatest number of affine dots. Let
r=\sum_{k=1}^{d}\beta_{k}(D_{1})
be the total number of affine dots in
D_{1}
. Let
\mathbf{b}^{\vee}
be defined as in
Eq.

10.6.3
using
D=D_{1}
. Let us consider the image of
H_{n}\left(\sum_{t=1}^{p}\nu_{t}D_{t}\right)_{\mathcal{M}}(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}})
in the summand of
Section

10.5
indexed by
\widetilde{h_{D_{1}}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}
.

If
D_{t}
has fewer than
r
affine dots, then by
Proposition

10.4.1

H_{n}\left(D_{t}\right)_{\mathcal{M}}(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}})=0
in
\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)^{\leq r}/\left(\mathcal{M}\otimes{}_{j_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{j_{d}}V\right)^{\leq(r-1)}
and does not contribute to the summand of interest. Without loss, we may assume
D_{1},\dotsc,D_{p}
each have exactly
r
affine dots.

Furthermore, by considering the multiplicity of each
h_{1},\dotsc,h_{n}
in
Proposition

10.4.1
we see that the projection of
H_{n}(D_{t})_{\mathcal{M}}\left(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}\right)
into the summand indexed by
\widetilde{h_{D_{1}}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}
is identically zero unless
\beta_{k}(D_{t})=\beta_{k}(D_{1})
for all
k=1,\dotsc,d
. That is, we may further assume that
D_{1},\dotsc,D_{p}
have exactly the same number of affine dots on each strand.

For these normally ordered diagrams, the image of
H_{n}(D_{t})_{\mathcal{M}}\left(1\otimes 1\otimes v_{1}^{i_{1}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{d}^{i_{d}}\right)
is given by Proposition
10.6.1
. For
a=1,\dotsc,p
, let
\alpha_{t,1},\dotsc\alpha_{t,d}\in\mathtt{B}
and
\tau_{t}\in S_{d}
be the notation for the normally ordered diagram
D_{t}
established in (
10.6.1
). Using this notation and Proposition
10.6.1
, the image in the summand of (
10.5
) indexed by
\widetilde{h_{D_{1}}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}
is given by

\sum_{t=1}^{p}K_{D_{t}}\nu_{t}\widetilde{h_{D_{1}}(\mathbf{b}^{\vee})}\otimes 1\otimes\left(v_{\tau_{t}^{-1}(1)}^{\alpha_{t,\tau_{t}^{-1}(1)}}\otimes v_{\tau_{t}^{-1}(2)}^{\alpha_{t,\tau_{t}^{-1}(2)}}\otimes\dotsb\otimes v_{\tau_{t}^{-1}(d)}^{\alpha_{t,\tau_{t}^{-1}(d)}}\right),

where
K_{D_{t}}\in\mathbbm{k}\setminus\{0\}
for
t=1,\dotsc,p
.
However, this is a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination of distinct basis elements of
X\otimes U(\mathfrak{u}^{-})\otimes{}_{i_{1}}V\otimes\dotsb\otimes{}_{i_{d}}V
as described in (
10.6.5
). From this we deduce
\nu_{t}=0
for
t=1,\dotsc,p
and the claim follows.
∎

Since the normally ordered diagrams span the morphism spaces of
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
, the following results immediately follow from the previous theorem.

Corollary 10.6.3
.

The family of functors
\{H_{n}\}_{n\geq 1}
is asymptotically faithful on
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
, meaning that on any fixed morphism in
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
, the functor
H_{n}
is faithful for
n
sufficiently large.

Corollary 10.6.4
.

The normally ordered diagrams give bases for the morphism spaces of
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
.

10.7.
The (degenerate) affine wreath product algebra

Savage has defined in
[
27
]
the
affine wreath product algebra

\mathcal{H}_{d}^{\textup{aff}}(A)
(we use this notation instead of Savage’s notation
\mathcal{A}_{d}(A)
to avoid confusion with our use of the symbol
\mathcal{A}
). Writing
\mathcal{H}^{\textup{aff}}(A):=\bigoplus_{\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}\in I^{d}}\mathbf{j}\mathcal{H}^{\textup{aff}}_{d}(A)\mathbf{i}
, we may view
\mathcal{H}^{\textup{aff}}(A)
as a monoidal
\mathbbm{k}
-supercategory with objects
\{\mathbf{i}\in I^{d}\mid d\in\mathbbm{Z}_{\geq 0}\}
. In view of
[
27
, Definition 3.1, Theorem 4.6]
, and Corollary
10.6.4
it is straightforward to check the following

Proposition 10.7.1
.

We have an isomorphism of monoidal categories
\mathcal{H}^{\textup{aff}}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
which sends (in Savage’s notation in
[
27
, Definition 3.1]
)
f_{r},x_{r},s_{r}
to the coupon
f
on the
r
th strand, the affine dot on the
r
th strand, and the crossing of the
r,r+1
strands, respectively.

Remark 10.7.2
.

In light of Proposition
10.7.1
, one may view
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}
as a ‘thickened’ analogue of the (degenerate) affine wreath product algebra.

11.
Asympototic faithfulness of the defining representation and a basis theorem

11.1.
A useful ordering on thin morphisms

Let
\mathbf{i}=i_{1}\cdots i_{d}
,
\mathbf{j}=j_{1}\cdots j_{d}
. We associate
\bm{\nu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j})
with data
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)
, where

\displaystyle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]=([t_{1},b_{1}],\ldots,[t_{d},b_{d}]),\qquad\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}

and
\nu_{u,\sigma u}([t_{u},b_{u}])=1
for all
u\in[1,d]
. For instance, if we take
\bm{\nu}=\hat{\bm{\mu}}
as in Example
6.3.1
, then we associate
\bm{\nu}
with

\displaystyle([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)=(([1,x],[1,x],[2,i],[2,i],[0,j],[0,y],[0,y],[0,y],[2,z],[1,j],[1,j],[1,z]),(3,4,5)).

We put a total order
\lessdot
on
\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j})
as follows. Choose any order on
\mathfrak{S}_{d}
which refines the Bruhat order to a total order. We say
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\lessdot([\mathbf{t}^{\prime},\mathbf{b}^{\prime}],\sigma^{\prime})
provided

(1)

|\mathbf{t}|<|\mathbf{t}^{\prime}|
(comparison of affine degrees), or;

(2)

|\mathbf{t}|=|\mathbf{t}^{\prime}|
and
\sigma>\sigma^{\prime}
(comparison in the Bruhat order), or;

(3)

|\mathbf{t}|=|\mathbf{t}^{\prime}|
,
\sigma=\sigma^{\prime}
, and
[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]<[\mathbf{t}^{\prime},\mathbf{b}^{\prime}]
in the lexicographic total order induced by the total order on
\mathtt{P}
as in §
6.2
.

We write

\displaystyle\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j})_{\lessdot\bm{\mu}}=\mathbbm{k}\{\eta_{\bm{\nu}}\mid\bm{\nu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}),\bm{\nu}\lessdot\bm{\mu}\}.

11.2.
Explosion and cabling

Recall the explosion map from §
3.4
and the morphisms
\eta_{\bm{\mu}}
and its cabled mate
\eta_{\hat{\bm{\mu}}}
from §
6.3
.

Lemma 11.2.1
.

Let
\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
.
We have
|\bm{\mu}|^{!}_{a}exp_{\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})}}(\eta_{\bm{\mu}})-|\bm{\mu}|^{!}\eta_{\hat{\bm{\mu}}}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff, thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{\mathbf{x}},\mathbf{j}^{\mathbf{y}})_{\lessdot\hat{\bm{\mu}}}
.

Proof.

Assume
\mathbf{i}^{(x)}=i_{1}^{(x_{1})}\cdots i_{m}^{(x_{m})}
and
\mathbf{j}^{(y)}=j_{1}^{(y_{1})}\cdots j_{n}^{(y_{n})}
.
We compute

11.3.
Asymptotic faithfulness and a basis for
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}

Theorem 11.3.1
.

The family of functors
\{H_{n}\}_{n\geq 1}
is asympotically faithful on
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}
. That is, for any given morphism space in
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}
the functor
H_{n}
is faithful for
n\gg 0
.

Proof.

We have that
\{\eta_{\bm{\mu}}\mid\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})\}
is a
\mathbbm{k}
-spanning set for
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
by Corollary
6.4.2
. Letting
0\neq\rho\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
, we have that

\displaystyle\rho=\sum_{\bm{\nu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})}c_{\bm{\nu}}\eta_{\bm{\nu}}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})

for some coefficients
c_{\bm{\nu}}\in\mathbbm{k}
, not all zero.
Let
\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
be chosen such that
c_{\bm{\mu}}\neq 0
and
\hat{\bm{\nu}}\lessdot\hat{\bm{\mu}}
for all
\bm{\nu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
with
\bm{\nu}\neq\bm{\mu}
and
c_{\bm{\nu}}\neq 0
. Take

\displaystyle C=\prod_{\begin{subarray}{c}\bm{\mu}\neq\bm{\nu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})\\
c_{\bm{\nu}}\neq 0\end{subarray}}|\bm{\nu}|^{!}_{\mathfrak{a}}\in\mathbbm{k}.

We have then by Lemma
11.2.1
that

\displaystyle C|\bm{\mu}|^{!}_{\mathfrak{a}}exp_{\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})}}(\rho)

\displaystyle=C|\bm{\mu}|^{!}_{\mathfrak{a}}\sum_{\bm{\nu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})}c_{\bm{\nu}}exp_{\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})}}(\eta_{\bm{\nu}})=C|\bm{\mu}|^{!}c_{\bm{\mu}}\eta_{\hat{\bm{\mu}}}+X,

where
X\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{\mathbf{x}},\mathbf{j}^{\mathbf{y}})_{\lessdot\hat{\bm{\mu}}}
. Thus Corollary
10.6.3
implies that there exists some
n\gg 0
such that

\displaystyle 0\neq H_{n}(C|\bm{\mu}|^{!}_{\mathfrak{a}}exp_{\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})}}(\rho))=C|\bm{\mu}|^{!}_{\mathfrak{a}}H_{n}(Y_{\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})}})\circ H_{n}(\rho)\circ H_{n}(Z_{\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})}}),

and thus
H_{n}(\rho)\neq 0
, completing the proof.
∎

We have the following corollary to (the proof of) Theorem
11.3.1
:

Corollary 11.3.2
.

The diagrams
\{\eta_{\bm{\mu}}\mid\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})\}
form a
\mathbbm{k}
-basis for
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
.

12.
The cyclotomic quotient category
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}

In this section we define cyclotomic quotients of the affine Frobenius web category
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}
, and establish a basis theorem for these objects.
Let
\mathbf{L}=(L_{1},\ldots,L_{t})\in\mathbbm{Z}_{>0}^{t}
and set
\ell=L_{1}+\cdots+L_{t}
. Let
\mathbf{c}=(c_{i,k})_{i\in I,k\in[1,t]}
be such that

(12.0.1)

\displaystyle c_{i,k}\in(iAi)_{\bar{0}}\qquad\textup{and}\qquad c_{j,k}x=\psi^{-L_{k}}(x)c_{i,k}

for all
k\in[1,t]
,
i,j\in I
and
x\in jAi
. Roughly speaking, the requirement on the right side of (
12.0.1
) ensures that
x
“commutes past the coupons
\{c_{j,k}\}
like it commutes past
k
affine dots”.
We call
\Lambda=(\mathbf{L},\mathbf{c})
a
cyclotomic datum
of
level
\ell
.

Let
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
be the quotient of
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
by the right tensor ideal

\displaystyle\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}:=\big\langle f_{i}\mid i\in I\big\rangle.

We will often make use of bars to indicate morphisms considered in the quotient category.
Under the isomorphism
\mathcal{H}^{\textup{aff}}(A)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
in
Proposition

10.7.1
, one may view
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
as a special case (for a much stricter type of cyclotomic datum) of Savage’s
cyclotomic wreath quotient algebra
(see
[
27
, Section 6.2]
).
Set

\displaystyle\mathcal{M}^{\Lambda}(\mathbf{i}^{(x)},\mathbf{j}^{(y)})=\{\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(x)},\mathbf{j}^{(y)})\mid\mu_{r,s}(t,b)=0\textup{ for all }t\geq\ell\},

In other words,
\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}^{\Lambda}(\mathbf{i}^{(x)},\mathbf{j}^{(y)})
only if
\eta_{\bm{\mu}}
carries at most
\ell-1
affine dots on any given strand (for example, for
\bm{\mu}
as in
Example

6.3.1
, we would have
\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}^{\Lambda}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
if and only if
\ell\geq 3
.
The next result follows from
Proposition

10.7.1
and
[
27
, Theorem 6.11]
:

Lemma 12.1.1
.

Let
\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j}\in I^{d}
. Then
\{\bar{\eta}_{\bm{\mu}}\mid\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}^{\Lambda}(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j})\}
is a
\mathbbm{k}
-basis for
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i},\mathbf{j})
.

12.2.

12.1.1

Remark 12.2.2
.

Empirically speaking, many choices of cyclotomic datum wind up being regular. But this is not always the case; a counterexample arises for instance in the case of the truncated polynomial algebra
A=A_{\bar{0}}=\mathbbm{Z}[x]/(x^{4})
,
\mathfrak{a}=\mathbbm{Z}\{1,x^{2}\}
, as discussed in
Section

2.2
, and cyclotomic datum
\Lambda=(\mathbf{L},\mathbf{c})
with
\mathbf{L}=(1)
,
\mathbf{c}=(x)
. It is easy to see that regularity fails when
d=2
.

Proposition 12.2.4
.

\iota^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}:\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}\rightarrow\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}

}{{{{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@transformcm{1.0}{0.0}{0.0}{1.0}{14.44672pt}{1.66418pt}\lxSVG@begingroup@{transform} \pgfsys@hbox{65}\lxSVG@closescope }}}

\lxSVG@closescope {\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}\hss}\lxSVG@discardpath\lxSVG@closescope \hss}}\lxSVG@closescope\endpgfpicture}}}$}}}}}}}}}=con_{i^{(d)},i^{(d)}}(F_{i}^{(d)}),

where
F_{i}^{(d)}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(i^{d},i^{d})
and
\overline{F}_{i}^{(d)}=0
in
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
by
Eq.

12.2.1
, so
F_{i}^{(d)}\in\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}
.

Now assume
n\geq d
,
\mathbf{j}=j_{1}\cdots j_{n},\mathbf{k}=k_{1}\cdots k_{n}\in I^{n}
. We consider any morphism of the form

(12.2.4)

\displaystyle Q_{3}\circ(f_{i}^{(d)}\otimes Q_{2})\circ Q_{1}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k}),

where
Q_{1}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{j},i^{(d)}\mathbf{p}^{(\mathbf{x})})
,
Q_{2}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{p}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{q}^{(\mathbf{y})})
, and
Q_{3}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(i^{(d)}\mathbf{q}^{(\mathbf{y})},\mathbf{k})
for some
\mathbf{p}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{q}^{(\mathbf{y})}\in\widehat{\Omega}
, noting that
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k})\cap\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda}
is
\mathbbm{k}
-spanned by such morphisms by definition. By the above paragraph we have

\displaystyle d!\;Q_{3}\circ(f_{i}^{(d)}\otimes Q_{2})\circ Q_{1}

\displaystyle=Q_{3}\circ(con_{i^{(d)},i^{(d)}}(F_{i}^{(d)})\otimes Q_{2})\circ Q_{1}

\displaystyle=Q_{3}^{\prime}\circ((exp_{i^{(d)},i^{(d)}}\circ con_{i^{(d)},i^{(d)}}(F_{i}^{(d)}))\otimes exp_{\mathbf{p}^{(x)},\mathbf{q}^{(y)}}(Q_{2})))\circ Q_{1}^{\prime}

for some
Q_{1}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{j},i^{d}\mathbf{p}^{\mathbf{x}})
and
Q_{3}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(i^{d}\mathbf{q}^{\mathbf{y}},\mathbf{k})
, thanks to Corollary
6.4.2
. Now, by Lemma
3.4.2
and Corollary
6.4.2
, the above is equal to

(12.2.5)

\displaystyle\sum_{\sigma,\omega\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}}Q_{3}^{\prime}\circ((\sigma\circ F_{i}^{(d)}\circ\omega)\otimes Q_{2}^{\prime})\circ Q_{1}^{\prime}

for some
Q_{2}^{\prime}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{p}^{\mathbf{x}},\mathbf{q}^{\mathbf{y}})
. Now note that each constituent morphism in (
12.2.5
) is in
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
, and therefore (
12.2.5
) is in
\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}
since
F_{i}^{(d)}\in\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}
. Thus
d!Q_{3}\circ(f_{i}^{(d)}\otimes Q_{2})\circ Q_{1}\in\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}
, so
Q_{3}\circ(f_{i}^{(d)}\otimes Q_{2})\circ Q_{1}\in\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}
since
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
is torsion-free by Lemma
12.1.1
.

Now, let
\rho\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k})
, and assume
\iota^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}(\bar{\rho})=0
. We have then that
\rho\in\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda}
. Since
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k})\cap\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda}
is spanned by morphisms of the form (
12.2.4
), we have then that
\rho\in\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}
by the above paragraph. Thus
\bar{\rho}=0\in\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{j},\mathbf{k})
initially, so
\iota^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}
is faithful, as required.
∎

Proposition 12.2.5
.

We have that

\{\overline{\eta}_{\bm{\mu}}\mid\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}^{\Lambda}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})\}

is a
\mathbbm{k}
-basis for
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
.

Proof.

First we prove spanning.
We have by
Corollary

6.4.2
that
\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
is a spanning set for
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
. Now, assume a diagram
D\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
has a strand which carries
\geq\ell
affine dots. We will show that we may write
\overline{D}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
as a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination of diagrams with lesser overall affine degree, and then the claim follows by induction.
Indeed, using
Eq.

5.1.3
, we may pull the strand with
\geq\ell
dots all the way to the left (modulo a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination of diagrams with lesser affine degree), and then use the cyclotomic relation
Eq.

12.2.3
to rewrite this diagram as a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination of diagrams with lesser affine degree, completing the spanning proof.

Now we prove independence.
Assume
\rho=\sum_{\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}^{\Lambda}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})}\gamma_{\bm{\mu}}\eta_{\bm{\mu}}\in\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})
is a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination such that not all coefficients
\gamma_{\bm{\mu}}
are zero. Let
\bm{\nu}
be such that
\hat{\bm{\nu}}
is maximally
\lessdot
-dominant with
\gamma_{\bm{\nu}}\neq 0
. Let
K=\prod_{\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}^{\Lambda}(\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})})}|\bm{\mu}|^{!}
.
Then by
Lemma

11.2.1
we have

\displaystyle C\overline{exp_{\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})}}(\rho)}-C^{\prime}\overline{\eta}_{\hat{\bm{\nu}}}\in{\mathbf{Web}}(\mathbf{i}^{\mathbf{x}},\mathbf{j}^{\mathbf{y}})_{\lessdot\hat{\bm{\mu}}}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}

for some
C^{\prime}\in\mathbbm{Z}_{\neq 0}
. By
Lemma

12.1.1
we have then that
\overline{exp_{\mathbf{i}^{(\mathbf{x})},\mathbf{j}^{(\mathbf{y})}}(\rho)}
is nonzero in
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}
, and thus
\bar{\rho}
is nonzero in
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}
by
Proposition

12.2.4
, completing the proof.
∎

Proposition

12.2.5
implies the immediate

Corollary 12.2.6
.

Let
\Lambda
be a regular cyclotomic datum of level
\ell=1
. Then we have an isomorphism of categories
\mathbf{Web}_{\mathcal{A}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}
which is the identity on objects and diagrams.

12.3.
Regularity and the thick cyclotomic quotient category in special cases

In general,
regularity
of a cyclotomic datum
\Lambda=(\mathbf{L},\mathbf{c})
and the explicit definition of the associated quotient ideal
\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda}
of
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}
requires direct computation. In this section we outline some cases where regularity can be established without computation.

12.3.1.
Regularity over a characteristic zero field

If
\mathbbm{k}
is a field of characteristic zero, then every morphism in
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}(i^{(d)},i^{(d)})
is divisible by
d!
, and hence any choice of cyclotomic datum
\Lambda
is regular and so
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}
is well-defined. Indeed, in this setting we have
\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda,\textup{thin}}=\mathcal{I}^{\Lambda}
as may be seen in the proof of
Proposition

12.2.4
.

12.3.2.
Regularity under some nice idempotent conditions

In the following proposition, we show that for various important classes of algebras
A
(see
Remark

12.3.2
), a natural choice of cyclotomic datum is regular, and we directly describe the associated quotient ideal (note that the below proposition places no extra conditions on the underlying ring
\mathbbm{k}
or the even subalgebra
\mathfrak{a}
).

Proposition 12.3.1
.

Assume
A
is such that
(i^{\vee})^{2}=0
and
i^{\vee}b=\delta_{b,i}i^{\vee}
for all
b\in\mathtt{B}
,
i\in I
, and
\Lambda=(\mathbf{L},\mathbf{c})
is such that
L_{k}=1
and
c_{i,k}=\gamma_{i,k}i^{\vee}
for all
i\in I,k\in[1,t]
, and some integers
\gamma_{i,k}\in\mathbbm{Z}\subseteq\mathbbm{k}
. Then
\Lambda
is regular, and the defining quotient ideal of
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}

The
absolute length

u(\sigma)
of a permutation
\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}
is the minimum number of (not necessarily simple) transpositions whose product is
\sigma
. It is a well-known fact that for
x\in\mathbbm{Z}
, we have

(12.3.2)

\displaystyle\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}}x^{d-u(\sigma)}=x(x+1)\cdots(x+d-1)=d!{x+d-1\choose d}.

,
12.2.3
),
Lemma

3.3.1
and (
12.3.2
).
∎

Remark 12.3.2
.

In many cases of interest (such as the zigzag algebras (see
Section

2.2.3
), or trivial extension algebras of quiver algebras more generally (see
Lemma

3.3.1
)), the algebra
A
is non-negatively graded, with the degree-zero component spanned by the orthogonal idempotents
I
, and with the trace map having degree
-m
for some
m\in\mathbbm{Z}_{>0}
. In this setting
Proposition

12.3.1
gives a direct construction of most natural choices of cyclotomic quotient categories
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}
.

Indeed, in this setting the top degree
m
component of
A
is spanned by the dual elements
I^{\vee}
, so
A
satisfies the first condition in
Proposition

12.3.1
. Moreover, in this setting,
\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff}}_{\mathcal{A}}
inherits a natural grading as well, taking the
x
-thick affine dot to have degree
xm
. Thus if one wants to construct a cyclotomic quotient
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}
which preserves this grading, the only coherent choices of cyclotomic datum are as presented in
Proposition

12.3.1
.

12.3.3.
Regularity in the
\mathfrak{a}=A_{\bar{0}}
case

In this section we prove that when
\mathfrak{a}=A_{\bar{0}}
,
every
choice of cyclotomic datum
\Lambda=(\mathbf{L},\mathbf{c})
is regular, and thus
\mathbf{Web}^{\Lambda}_{\mathcal{A}}
is well-defined. Understanding the explicit definition of the cyclotomic ideal
\mathcal{I}^{\Gamma}
still requires computation in general.

Throughout this subsection we assume
\mathfrak{a}=A_{\bar{0}}
. Note that the symmetric group
\mathfrak{S}_{d}
acts on the left of
W_{d,i}:=\mathbf{Web}^{\textup{aff},\textup{thin}}_{\mathcal{A}}(i^{d},i^{d})
by conjugating diagrams:

\displaystyle\omega\cdot\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 55.70233pt\hbox{{\hbox{\kern-55.70233pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-2.77223pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\begin{overpic}[WebAffImages/CONJ1.pdf]
\put(12.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(67.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(12.0,101.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(67.0,101.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(40.0,10.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(40.0,90.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(42.0,50.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle D$}}
\end{overpic}}$}}}}}}}}}\;\;=\;\;\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 67.20541pt\hbox{{\hbox{\kern-67.20541pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-2.77223pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\begin{overpic}[WebAffImages/CONJ2.pdf]
\put(12.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(67.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(12.0,101.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(67.0,101.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(40.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(40.0,101.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(40.0,50.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle D$}}
\put(40.0,22.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\omega$}}
\put(40.0,78.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\omega^{-1}$}}
\end{overpic}}$}}}}}}}}}

We write
W_{d,i}^{\mathfrak{S}_{d}}
for the
\mathfrak{S}_{d}
-invariants in
W_{d,i}
. By
Corollary

10.6.4
we have that
W_{d,i}
has
\mathbbm{k}
-basis given by normally-ordered diagrams of the form

\displaystyle\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\hbox{{}}}}}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}:=\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 63.98688pt\hbox{{\hbox{\kern-63.98688pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-2.59723pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\begin{overpic}[WebAffImages/CONJ3.pdf]
\put(15.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(85.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(15.0,92.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(85.0,92.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(50.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(50.0,101.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(50.0,62.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\sigma$}}
\put(50.0,27.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]$}}
\end{overpic}}$}}}}}}}}}=\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 81.07294pt\hbox{{\hbox{\kern-81.07294pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-2.59723pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\begin{overpic}[WebAffImages/CONJ3x.pdf]
\put(15.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(85.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[t]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(15.0,65.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(85.0,65.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0)[b]{$\scriptstyle i^{(1)}$}}
\put(50.0,-1.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(50.0,65.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\cdots$}}
\put(50.0,45.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle\sigma$}}
\put(20.0,20.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle[t_{1},b_{1}]$}}
\put(80.0,20.0){\pic@makebox@{\makebox}{}(0.0,0.0){$\scriptstyle[t_{d},b_{d}]$}}
\end{overpic}}$}}}}}}}}}

where
\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}
and
[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]=([t_{1},b_{1}],\ldots,[t_{d},b_{d}])\in{}_{i}\mathtt{P}_{i}^{d}
,
indexing the basis morphisms for
W_{d,i}
using the nomenclature in
Section

11.1
.
We write
Y_{d,i}:=\{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\mid[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]\in{}_{i}\mathtt{P}_{i}^{d},\sigma\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}\}
for the indexing set of these normally-ordered diagrams. (We of course have
\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}=\eta_{\bm{\mu}}
for some
\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(i^{d},i^{d})
, but in this section it will be more convenient to index via
Y_{d,i}
).

There is a left
\mathfrak{S}_{d}
-action on
\pm Y_{d,i}
by

\displaystyle([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)^{\omega}:=(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}];\omega\rangle}([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\omega},\sigma^{\omega})=(-1)^{\langle\mathbf{b};\omega\rangle}(([t_{\omega 1},b_{\omega 1}],\ldots,[t_{\omega d},b_{\omega d}],\omega\sigma\omega^{-1}),

where

\displaystyle\langle\mathbf{b};\omega\rangle=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}r<s\\
\omega r>\omega s\end{subarray}}\bar{b}_{r}\bar{b}_{s}.

For
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in Y_{d,i}
, write:

\displaystyle\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}

\displaystyle:=\{\omega\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}\mid([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)^{\omega}=([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\}

\displaystyle\mathfrak{S}^{\pm}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}

\displaystyle:=\{\omega\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}\mid([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)^{\omega}=\pm([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\}

\displaystyle\mathcal{O}^{\pm}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}

\displaystyle:=\{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\mid([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)^{\omega}=\pm([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\}.

We designate by
\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
a set of minimal coset representatives for
\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\backslash\mathfrak{S}_{d}
, and we designate by
\mathscr{D}^{\pm}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
a set of minimal coset representatives for
\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}^{\pm}\backslash\mathfrak{S}_{d}
.

We choose an ordering
\succ
on
Y_{d,i}
such that
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\succ([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})
provided:

(1)

t_{1}+\cdots+t_{d}>t_{1}^{\prime}+\cdots+t_{d}^{\prime}
(i.e.
(([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)
has higher affine degree than
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})
), or;

(2)

t_{1}+\cdots+t_{d}=t_{1}^{\prime}+\cdots+t_{d}^{\prime}
, and
[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]>[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime}
in the lexicographic order induced by the total order on
{}_{i}\mathtt{P}_{i}
, or;

(3)

[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]=[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime}
and
\omega>\omega^{\prime}
.

Note that
\prec
is slightly different than the order
\lessdot
on
Y_{d,i}
defined in
Section

11.1
, and is more useful for the purposes of this section.
Under the ordering
\prec
, every orbit
\mathcal{O}^{\pm}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
has a unique dominant member. We write

\displaystyle\hat{Y}_{d,i}^{\pm}=\{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in Y_{d,i}\mid([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\textup{ is $\prec$-dominant in }\mathcal{O}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}^{\pm}\}.

Note that if
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}^{\pm}
, then
[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]=([t_{j_{1}},b_{j_{1}}]^{m_{1}},\ldots,[t_{j_{q}},b_{j_{q}}]^{m_{q}})
for some
q,m_{1},\ldots,m_{q}>0
, where
[t_{j_{r}},b_{j_{r}}]>[t_{j_{s}},b_{j_{s}}]
if
r<s
. Writing
\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}:=\mathfrak{S}_{m_{1}}\times\cdots\times\mathfrak{S}_{m_{q}}
, note that we have
\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\leq\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}
.
Finally, define

\displaystyle\hat{Y}_{d,i}:=\{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}^{\pm}\mid\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}=\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}^{\pm}\}.

Lemma 12.3.3
.

Let
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in Y_{d,i}
.

(1)

We have that
\omega^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\omega=(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}];\omega\rangle}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\omega},\sigma^{\omega})}
modulo terms of lower affine degree.

(2)

We have
\omega^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\omega=\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
if
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}
and
\omega\in\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
.

Proof.

(1) is obvious from relations in
W_{d,i}
. For (2), note that if
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}
, then
\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}<\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}
, so by
Lemma

5.3.1
we have

\displaystyle\omega^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\omega

\displaystyle=\omega^{-1}\eta_{(i^{d},\sigma)}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\textup{id})}\omega=\omega^{-1}\eta_{(i^{d},\sigma)}\omega\circ\omega^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\textup{id})}\omega

\displaystyle=\eta_{(i^{d},\sigma)}\circ(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}];\omega\rangle}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\textup{id})}=\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)},

where
(-1)^{\langle([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\rangle}=1
since
\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}=\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}^{\pm}
.
∎

Now, for
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}
, we define:

\displaystyle\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}=\sum_{\tau\in\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}}\tau^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\tau\in W_{d,i}.

Lemma 12.3.4
.

For all
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}
, we have that
\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\in W_{d,i}^{\mathfrak{S}_{d}}
and
\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}-\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
is a
\mathbbm{k}
-linear combination of terms of the form
\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}
, where
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\prec([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)
.

Proof.

Let
\omega\in\mathfrak{S}_{d}
. For each
\tau\in\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
, there exists
\tau_{\omega}\in\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
,
\nu_{\omega}\in\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
such that
\tau\omega=\nu_{\omega}\tau_{\omega}
. Then we have

\displaystyle\omega^{-1}\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\omega

\displaystyle=\sum_{\tau\in\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}}\omega^{-1}\tau^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\tau\omega=\sum_{\tau\in\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}}\tau_{\omega}^{-1}\nu_{\omega}^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\nu_{\omega}\tau_{\omega}

\displaystyle=\sum_{\tau\in\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}}\tau_{\omega}^{-1}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\tau_{\omega}=\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)},

where the last equality follows from
Lemma

12.3.3
(ii). This proves the first claim. For the second claim, note that by
Lemma

12.3.3
(i), we have the following equalities modulo the
\mathbbm{k}
-span of terms of the form
\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}
with lower affine degree than
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)
:

\displaystyle\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}

\displaystyle\equiv\sum_{\tau\in\mathscr{D}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}}(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}];\tau\rangle}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\tau},\sigma^{\tau})}\equiv\sum_{\tau\in\mathscr{D}^{\pm}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}}(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}];\tau\rangle}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\tau},\sigma^{\tau})}

\displaystyle\equiv\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}+\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\in\mathcal{O}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}^{\pm}\\
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})\neq([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\end{subarray}}c_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})},

for some
c_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}\in\mathbbm{k}
. Since
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}
, it is the most dominant member of
\mathcal{O}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}^{\pm}
, proving the claim.
∎

Lemma 12.3.5
.

We have
W_{d,i}^{\mathfrak{S}_{d}}=\mathbbm{k}\{\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\mid([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}\}
.

Proof.

Let
z\in W_{d,i}^{\mathfrak{S_{d}}}
. By
Lemma

12.3.4
it is enough to show that
z\in\mathbbm{k}\{\xi_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\mid([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}\}
. By
Corollary

10.6.4
we may write
z=\sum_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)\in S}p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}+q
, where
S\subseteq Y_{d,i}
is a subset of elements of equal maximal affine degree, and
q
is a sum of terms of lower affine degree.

Claim I: If
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)
is such that
p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}\neq 0
, then
\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}=\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}^{\pm}
.
To see this, assume not. Then there exists
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})
with
p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}\neq 0
and
\omega\in\mathfrak{S}^{\pm}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}\backslash\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}
. By
Lemma

12.3.3
(i),
\omega^{-1}z\omega\equiv\sum p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}];\omega\rangle}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\omega},\sigma^{\omega})}
modulo terms of lower affine degree. Now,
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})=(([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime})^{\omega},(\sigma^{\prime})^{\omega})
, so
\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}
arises with coefficient
p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}
in
z
, and with coefficient
(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\omega^{\prime}\rangle}p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}=-p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\prime},\sigma^{\prime})}
in
\omega^{-1}z\omega
. But
z=\omega^{-1}z\omega
, giving the desired contradiction and proving Claim I.

Now, let
([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)\in S
be
\prec
-maximal such that
p_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)}\neq 0
.

Claim II: We have
([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)\in\hat{Y}_{d,i}
.
To see this, assume not. Then there exists a more
\prec
-dominant
([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}]^{\omega},\epsilon^{\omega})\in\mathcal{O}_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)}^{\pm}
. Then by
Lemma

12.3.3
(i), we have that
\omega^{-1}z\omega\equiv\sum(-1)^{\langle[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}];\omega\rangle}p_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\omega)}\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]^{\omega},\sigma^{\omega})}
modulo terms of lower affine degree. The coefficient of
\eta_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}]^{\omega},\epsilon^{\omega})}
in
\omega^{-1}z\omega
is
\pm p_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)}\neq 0
, which contradicts the
\prec
-maximality of
([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)
since
\omega^{-1}z\omega=z
and proves Claim II.

Finally, we have by
Lemma

12.3.4
that
z-p_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)}\xi_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)}\in W_{d,i}^{\mathfrak{S}_{d}}
, and
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)<([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)
for any
([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)
such that
\eta_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}
arises in the support of
z-p_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)}\xi_{([\mathbf{u},\mathbf{d}],\epsilon)}
. The lemma statement then follows by induction on the dominance order on
Y_{d,i}
.
∎

Proposition 12.3.6
.

Assume
\Lambda=(\mathbf{L},\mathbf{c})
is a cyclotomic datum for
\mathcal{A}=(A,A_{\bar{0}})
. Then
\Lambda
is regular.

Proof.

Considering (
12.2.1
), it follows from
Lemma

5.3.1
and
Lemma

12.3.5
that

(12.3.4)

\displaystyle\sum_{\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(i^{d},i^{d})_{<\ell}}\kappa^{\Lambda,d,i}_{\bm{\mu}}\overline{\eta}_{\bm{\mu}}=\underbrace{\lx@xy@svg{\hbox{\raise 2.5pt\hbox{\kern 29.09727pt\hbox{{\hbox{\kern-29.09727pt\raise 0.0pt\hbox{\hbox{\kern 0.0pt\raise-29.09686pt\hbox{$\textstyle{\hbox to58.2pt{\vbox to58.19pt{\pgfpicture\makeatletter\hbox{\hskip 10.42365pt\lower-17.41016pt\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} \lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke} \lxSVG@begingroup@{fill} \lxSVG@setlinewidth{\the\pgflinewidth}\lxSVG@begingroup@{stroke-width} \lx@inpgf@ignorespaces\nullfont\hbox to0.0pt{\lxSVG@begingroup@{_scopebegin} {{\lx@inpgf@ignorespaces}}

where
\bm{\mu}\in\mathcal{M}(i^{(d)},i^{(d)})
is the composition such that

\displaystyle\bm{\mu}([m_{r},t_{r}])=\#\{u\mid[m_{u},t_{u}]=[m_{r},t_{r}]\}

for all
r\in[1,t]
. In essence, we get the last equality above by closing up all the knotholes with identical coupons and dots, which we may do given the assumption that
\mathfrak{a}=A_{\bar{0}}
. Now note that

\displaystyle[\mathfrak{S}_{d}:\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}]\cdot|\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}|

\displaystyle=[\mathfrak{S}_{d}:\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}]\cdot[\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}:\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}]\cdot|\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}|

\displaystyle=|\mathfrak{S}_{d}|\cdot[\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}:\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}]=d![\mathfrak{S}_{[\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}]}:\mathfrak{S}_{([\mathbf{t},\mathbf{b}],\sigma)}].

Thus it follows from (
12.2.3
) that
\Lambda
is regular.
∎
